domain_restrictions: n is an integer and satisfies n > 1
m is an integer and satisfies 0 <= m <= n - 2
x is a real number whenever f_n(x) is evaluated
the sums use integer index k with k between 1 and n inclusive
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For each integer n > 1, if H_n is defined as the sum from k = 1 to n of 1 divided by k, and f_n is defined by f_n(x) equals the floor of n times x minus the sum from k = 1 to n of (the floor of k times x) divided by k, then for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n - 2, f_n of (m divided by n) is strictly less than H_n minus 1.
quantifier_order: for each integer n with n > 1
for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n - 2

variables.name: n
variables.role: global parameter used to define H_n and the function f_n

variables.name: f_n
variables.role: depends on n and is evaluated at x

variables.name: x
variables.role: input to f_n; used inside floor(n*x) and floor(k*x)

variables.name: m
variables.role: quantified variable in the inequality, specialized as x = m/n

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index for sums from k = 1 to k = n

witness_dependencies: no existential witnesses are asserted; the bound holds for all allowed m with x fixed as m/n

statement_nl: Let n > 1, define H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k, and let f_n be defined by f_n(x) = floor(n*x) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k*x)/k. For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-2, one has f_n(m/n) < H_n - 1.
